parole.significato: A peasant, farmer or agricultural laborer in the Middle East and North Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فَلَّاح (fallāḥ, “peasant”), from Classical Syriac ܦܠܚܐ (“worker; peasant”). Attested since 1743.

parole.significato: A medieval Arab condiment made from fermented barley.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic مُرِّيّ (murriyy), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܡܘܼܪܝܵܐ (mūryā, “brine”), borrowed from Latin muria (“brine, salty pickling solution”).

parole.significato: A concept of virtue and honor within a family, typically relating to chastity of female family members.
parole.testo: From Arabic نَامُوس (nāmūs). Doublet of nome and nomos.

parole.significato: Fasting, abstention, abstinence; the third of the five pillars of Islam.
parole.testo: From Arabic صَوْم (ṣawm, “fasting; abstaining from food, drink, and sex”), probably borrowed from Classical Syriac ܨܘܡܐ (ṣawmāʾ).

parole.significato: A particular herb, similar in flavor to thyme or oregano, used in Middle Eastern cuisine (Origanum syriacum).
parole.testo: From Arabic زَعْتَر (zaʕtar), صَعْتَر (ṣaʕtar, “wild thyme; condiment made from this herb”), probably from Classical Syriac ܨܬܪܐ (ṣāṯrā), related to Hebrew צַתְרָה (ṣátrā).
